sentences.text: This Appeal is directed against judgement and decree dated 14 th July 2014 passed by Principal District Judge, Kargil, in a civil suit bearing File no.25/suit titled as Mohammad Hussain and others v. Union of India and others and for setting aside the same.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 2. I have heard learned counsel for parties and considered the matter.

3. Learned counsel for appellant would contend that respondents/ plaintiffs have settled acquisition through private negotiations and have also received agreed compensation rendering the matter as settled.

According to him the issue with regard to claim for trees, buildings and machinery etc., has been settled by the Supreme Court in Mohanji and another v. State of U.P. and others, JT 1995 (8)
SC 599 , by holding that land owners or interested persons would be entitled to claim Page 1 compensation for these items by seeking reference under and terms of provisions of Section 18 of the State Land Acquisition Act,1990 (1934 A.D.) inasmuch as contesting respondents had remedy to claim compensation for the trees in accordance with the law and suit for damages was not maintainable before the Trial Court as the remedy was available under Section 5 and 18 of the Act.

sentences.text: While going through impugned judgement, it is evident at page 17 thereof that the Trial Court had gone through the record with regard to acquisition process that it called for perusal, from which it was found that Notices under Section 4 and 9 of the Act had been issued and thereafter parties had entered into private negotiations.

If that being the position, it means that the proceedings under and in terms of provisions of the Land Acquisition Act had been set in motion, acted upon and concluded by the parties by entering into private negotiations and as a corollary thereof, if any grievance that respondents/plaintiffs felt to have not been redressed, the same could have been agitated under and in terms of the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act and not by filing a Suit for damages and compensation.
5. Section 5 of the Act relates to payment for damage.
"5. Payment of damage.-- The officer so authorised shall at the time of such entry pay or tender payment for all necessary damage to be done as aforesaid, and, in case of dispute as to the sufficiency of the amount so paid or tendered, he shall at once refer the dispute to the Provincial Revenue authority within thirty days of its being pronounced, whereupon the decision of that officer shall be final."

Section 5 of the Act provides that the officer authorized shall at the time of such entry pay or tender payment for all necessary damage to be done and in case of dispute as to the sufficiency of the amount so Page 2 paid or tendered, he shall at once refer the dispute to the Provincial Revenue Authority whereupon the decision of that officer shall be final.

6. Insofar as Section 18 of the Act is concerned, it provides for making reference to the Court for determination of any objection relating to compensation, measurement of land or apportionment of compensation.

It would be, thus, appropriate to reproduce Section 18 hereunder:
"18. Reference to Court.

--
(1) Any person interested who has not accepted the award may, by written application to the Collector require that the matter be referred by the Collector for the determination of the Court, whether his objection be to the measurement of the land,
the amount of the compensation, the persons to whom it is payable or the apportionment of the compensation among the persons interested.

(2) The application shall state the grounds on which objection to the award is taken:
Provided that every such application shall be made.

--
(a) if the person making it was present or represented before the Collector at the time when he made his award, within six weeks from the date of the Collector's award;

2 (b) in other cases, within six weeks of the receipt of the notice from the Collector under section 12, sub-section (2), or within six months from the date of the Collector's award, whichever period shall first expire."

sentences.text:
7. Therefore, Section 18 of the Act provides that any person interested, who has not accepted the award, may make an application to Collector requiring him to make a reference for determination of the Court as regards his objection to the measurement of the land, the amount of the compensation,
the persons to whom it is payable or the apportionment of the compensation among the persons interested.

Consequently, it is no more res integra that civil courts have no jurisdiction to entertain suits relating to land acquisition proceedings, which could be justified only under Article 226 of the Constitution of India before the High Court.

It may not be out of place to mention here that the rulings of the Supreme Court are binding not only on High Courts, but also on all civil Page 3 courts in the country from entertaining any doubt regarding this proposition that the civil courts have no jurisdiction to entertain any suit relating to land acquisition matters.

8. Needless to mention that in the instant case, the subject is directly concerned with the land acquisition proceedings and land proceedings as admitted by the Trial Court itself had been finalized during private negotiations.

The suit has been entertained, tried and decreed by the Trial Court notwithstanding the fact that it lacks jurisdiction and the impugned judgement and decree rendered by it is absolutely bereft of any legal force.
9. In result, the Appeal succeeds and the same is, accordingly, allowed.

The judgement and decree dated 14th July 2014 passed by Principal District Judge, Kargil, in civil suit bearing File no.25/suit titled as Mohammad Hussain and others v. Union of India and others , is set-
